page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. CPU cache levels consist of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is locally attached via a 400 GB NVMe SSD. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain a dedicated GPU accelerator.

Instruction set features on this instance include AVX-512 foundations such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI. In synthetic benchmarking, the processor achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution and PassMark memory testing. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth rates are strong, recording 247.43 GB/sec in read operations and 159.49 GB/sec in write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression also places in the top quartile at 31.92 GB/sec. Broader multi-core compute tests, including Geekbench multi-core (8,916) and PassMark CPU (22,466.05), fall into the median performance tier.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation creates resource density favorable for memory-constrained workloads without requiring the purchase of higher core counts. Parallel computing throughput is constrained by the 8-thread ceiling, as observed in average multi-threaded decompression and lower prompt-processing rates on 7B parameter models. Given these specifications, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching systems, backend database operations, and data processing tasks requiring fast local NVMe storage.
